title: Shapes without inheritance
description:
In milestone 8 the shapes shared a base class and virtual functions. When the set of types is **fixed and known**, a `std::variant` does the same job with plain structs: no base class, no heap, no pointers.

The three structs and the `Shape` alias are provided. Write:

- `double area(const Shape& shape)` (circle: 3.14159 × r²; rectangle: w × h; triangle: b × h ÷ 2)
- `std::string name(const Shape& shape)`: `"circle"`, `"rectangle"`, `"triangle"`
- `std::tuple<std::string, double> largest(const std::vector<Shape>& shapes)`: the name and area of the biggest shape, or `{ "none", 0.0 }` for an empty list. The caller unpacks it with `auto [name, area]{ largest(shapes) };`
hints: `area` and `name` are each one `std::visit` with three lambdas, one per struct.
For `largest`, loop over the shapes keeping the best area and its name, then `return { bestName, bestArea };`.
